messages:
Cassie: Quick thread — proposing env-aware TTL + a short warm window before archiving traces to object store. Goal: cut dev/stage costs without hurting prod debug UX
Rahul: Sounds sensible. main worry is query latency for support lookups if we archive too aggressively :thinking_face:
Mina: can we do per-tenant overrides instead of env-only? some customers need longer retention even in staging
Cassie: yes per-tenant overrides are in scope but want a sane default first. proposal: prod warm window 30d, then archive; staging 7d warm, 30d archive; dev 3d warm, 14d archive
Jorge: how will archiving affect traces index? we have traceid->s3 pointer indexing today. if we move >30d to cold, querying entire trace means fetch from object store and rehydrate, adding seconds to lookup
Priya: on the Console side we can show a faded timeline and a one-click rehydrate action. want to avoid surprise timeouts in support flows
Mina: important to quantify cost + latency tradeoffs. can we simulate N lookups/week * rehydrate cost for support cases to see break-even
Cassie: agreed. also thinking about sampling vs TTL. for noisy services we can aggressively sample long-tail spans then keep full traces for errors only
Jorge: exporter-level hooks might help. we could attach a trace-level policy tag so collector routes heavy traces to warm retention and samples others to cold directly
Mina: that means changing OTLP collector routing. sample config snippet i sketched:

```yaml
processors:
  routing:
    rules:
      - from: attributes.service
        match: my-noisy-service
        action: tag_keep_full

exporters:
  cold_storage:
    endpoint: s3://traces-archive
  warm_index:
    endpoint: es://trace-index

extensions:
  ttl_manager:
    default_warm: 30d
    env_overrides:
      staging: 7d
      dev: 3d
```

Cassie: we also need a migration plan for existing 90d prod traces — can't move them all at once. propose staged rollouts by shard + monitor query 95th p50 rehydration times
Rahul: also quota interactions. if a customer has a small commit but spikes queries, rehydrates could blow dedicated quotas or cause regen storms
Priya: console UX: add a banner when a trace is archived and a small CTA rehydrate. also telemetry event when rehydrate invoked so we can bill or throttle if needed
Jorge: infra note: indexer memory usage drops if we remove old spans but index compaction job will be heavy during migration. schedule low-traffic windows
infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for ttl-manager feature branch — ci passed, canary target: trace-indexer-canary-2
Mina: next steps: run cost simulation for 3 policy variants (env-only, env+tenant overrides, sampler-based hybrid), estimate query latency impact, and mock Console rehydrate flow
Cassie: i'll open a short RFC with those sims + rollout playbook. tagging @Rahul @Priya for SLA and UX review. thanks everyone
Rahul: ack, will add quota/alert scenarios
Priya: ack, i'll mock the banner + rehydrate flow and share screenshots
Jorge: will plan indexer compaction windows and monitor canary
Cassie: timeline aim: decision by next Thurs so we can include in Q2 infra sprint
